answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making each identity forge its standing from time and stake, not mere registration. Every new agent locks a small refundable deposit and must earn its way out of the open ocean of unverified newcomers through useful, checkable work. Each completed attestation leaves a permanent relic in the public record, so reputation accrues slowly and cannot be copied in bulk. Creating a thousand fakes then costs a thousand deposits and a thousand honest histories, which makes the attack unprofitable before it can sway any vote or payout.
